Lessons.Title: Solving Systems by Substitution
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning objective: choose a conveniently isolated variable or expression, substitute it into another equation, solve and verify the pair against both original equations. Independently authored Edulytiks lesson based on Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U02:L13, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/2/13/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). Building On 8.EE.B.6 and HSA-REI.D.10; Addressing HSA-REI.C.6.

Original system: y=2x+1 and 3x+y=16. Substitute the entire expression 2x+1 into the second equation: 3x+(2x+1)=16, so 5x=15 and x=3; then y=7. The pair (3,7) checks both. Substitution can also be done using a value for x or another solved expression; choose a form that keeps arithmetic simple.

Another original system x=4, 2x+3y=20 yields 8+3y=20, y=4. A third example has the line y=−x+5 and equation 2x+y=8, producing x=3,y=2. Contrast systems where y is already isolated with systems requiring rearrangement first.

Student task: work one system by two substitution pathways, annotate which expression is replacing which variable, and check each final pair with the original constraints. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each for correct substitution, equation-solving steps, back-substitution checks and explanatory method choice.

KeyConcepts.Title: Substitution
KeyConcepts.Definition: Replace a variable with another expression known to equal it.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use parentheses when replacing a variable with a sum.

KeyConcepts.Title: Efficient variable choice
KeyConcepts.Definition: Choose an isolated variable or simple coefficient to reduce algebra.
KeyConcepts.Example: When x=4, substitute immediately rather than solving y first.

KeyConcepts.Title: Back-check
KeyConcepts.Definition: The final ordered pair must make both original equations true.

WorkedExamples.Title: Substitute an expression
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve y=2x+1, 3x+y=16.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each mathematical move and verify the result in the original equations.
Steps: Replace y by 2x+1 in second equation.

WorkedExamples.Title: Substitute a numeric value
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve x=4, 2x+3y=20.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each mathematical move and verify the result in the original equations.

WorkedExamples.Title: Use opposite-slope line
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve y=−x+5 and 2x+y=8.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each mathematical move and verify the result in the original equations.
WorkedExamples.Check: The substituted expression and final pair satisfy both equations.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Substituting only one term of an expression
CommonMistakes.Correction: Enclose a sum in parentheses during replacement.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Checking only the substituted one-variable equation
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: An arithmetic error might still produce a plausible x value.

SummaryPoints: Substitution replaces a variable with a known equal value or expression.
Choose the variable that is already isolated when possible.
An ordered pair is valid only if both original equations hold.
Teacher-scored explanations and alternate pathways remain important.
